{{Short description|American zoologist (1957–2010)}}
'''John Björn Thorbjarnarson''' (March 23, 1957 &ndash; February 14, 2010)<ref>{{cite news|title=John Thorbjarnarson, a Crocodile and Alligator Expert, Is Dead at 52|first=Douglas|last=Martin|date=March 7, 2010|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/10/science/10thorbjarnarson.html|accessdate=March 10, 2010}}</ref> was an Icelandic [[crocodilia]] [[Conservation biology|conservationist]] known for helping rescue numerous species from the brink of extinction.  Thorbjarnarson attended [[Cornell University]], and in 1991 he received his Ph.D. from the [[University of Florida]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Schaffer|first=Chuck|title=Remembering John Thorbjarnarson|url=http://www.expeditioncargo.com/conservation/remembering-john-thorbjarnarson|publisher=Expedition Cargo|accessdate=20 April 2013}}</ref> Thorbjarnarson was a conservation officer for the Wildlife Conservation Society in [[Gainesville, Florida]] for 19 years. He sought to preserve crocodile populations in [[Cuba]] (where he spent more than a decade doing research) and [[Brazil]], and to educate people about crocodiles and to ameliorate some of their fear. Thorbjarnarson traveled around the world and visiting swamps to help endangered reptiles after discovering that 23 species were in decline in 1988.<ref>{{cite news|title=John Thorbjarnarson|url=https://www.economist.com/obituary/2010/03/18/john-thorbjarnarson|publisher=TheEconomist.|access-date=20 April 2013|date=March 20, 2010}}</ref> He traveled to Asia, Africa, and Latin America to protect endangered species,<ref>{{cite web|title=WCS Mourns Loss of Dr. John Thorbjarnarson |url=http://www.wcs.org/news-and-features-main/thorbjarnarson-obit.asp |publisher=wcs|accessdate=20 April 2013}}</ref> visiting more than 30 countries in total.<ref>{{cite news|last=DOUGLAS|first=MARTIN|title=John Thorbjarnarson, a Crocodile and Alligator Expert, Is Dead at 52|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/03/10/science/10thorbjarnarson.html?_r=0|work=New York Times|accessdate=20 April 2013|date=March 9, 2010}}</ref> Thorbjarnarson wrote a book called ''The Chinese Alligator: Ecology, Behavior, Conservation, and Culture'', which talks about how the [[Chinese alligator]] is very important to the Chinese culture and history, including information about its relation to the Chinese dragon legend, as well as the biology and behavior of the species.<ref>{{cite web|last=Schaffer|first=Chuck|title=Remembering John Thorbjarnarson|url=http://www.expeditioncargo.com/conservation/remembering-john-thorbjarnarson|publisher=Expedition Cargo|accessdate=April 15, 2013}}</ref> Thorbjarnarson died of [[Plasmodium falciparum|falciparum]] [[malaria]] on February 14, 2010. Thorbjarnarson's family set up a foundation for The Wildlife Conservation Society.
